conventions.axes: As alts-2026-10-03.json: metres, origin on the floor at the back wall on the v3 sofa axis, X right as seen by the main camera, Y from back wall toward camera, Z up. Rig mirrored (scale.x = -1).
conventions.yaw_deg_left: Camera heading from -Y, positive = turned toward -X. f = (-sin yaw, -cos yaw, 0), r = (cos yaw, -sin yaw, 0).
conventions.armchair_local: Armchair local axes (yaw -25): lx (front) = (0.906, -0.423) = camera r; ly (sitter's left) = (0.423, 0.906) = -camera f. So u depends on lx only through x, and ly only changes depth: u = 0.52 + 0.6667 (x_c + lx)/(d_c - ly). The chair is seen in exact side profile.
conventions.tangent_rule: Two silhouette edges, a silhouette edge and a straight architectural line (jamb, mullion, corner, curtain stack edge, sill, table-top slab), or a silhouette edge and the frame edge: >= 0.02 apart, or crossing decisively (>= 0.02 overlap past the far edge). A vertical line crossing an inclined contour segment is a crossing, not a tangent; a vertical line within 0.02 of a contour corner or a near-vertical edge is a tangent.
conventions.window_lines: Measure the mullion and glass edges at the frame plane (outer face of the 0.35 reveal, X = -2.65), not at the wall face. In the B clay the mullion reads at u 0.259-0.266 (wall-face projection 0.295-0.301 is not visible). The front opening edge (u 0.191) is behind the front curtain stack; the visible line there is the stack edge (u ~0.203).

checks.note: report; accepted by design (master-designer, review-designer 8.7). Both are floor-contact lines; the basket stands 2 cm behind the rug's back-right corner (X 1.65, Y 0.72), whose projection (u 0.901, v 0.795) falls on the basket foot. Here 1 m of depth is only ~0.077 in v, so a clear 0.02 gap needs ~0.5 m of movement (cm moves change dv by <= 0.003; basket +2 cm X changes it by < 0.001). The basket cannot move back (lamp base) and the rug is firm. Render rule instead: the rug's pile edge passes in front of the basket foot, with the basket's own soft contact shadow on the parquet between them; never let the rug edge look like it runs under or through the basket.
